answer: The right defense turns identity into recurring, checkable work. Each new identity needs two sponsors from separate standing groups, both listed in the hollow registry. Sponsors lock security in the pulse pool that is confiscated if a random audit finds the recruit's work copied or empty. First rewards stay escrowed in the forge ledger until three unrelated peers verify a real task receipt. A ring cannot bootstrap itself: N fake identities require N independent sponsors with clean histories and money at risk, so headcount carries a capital cost, not just a registration fee.
